issues.item: Triggers: Being Followed: Feeling followed or tracked
issues.explanation: 'Being followed or tracked' is difficult to reconcile with the stated trauma type of trauma to a loved one and with the rest of the profile, which centers on grief, guilt, and generalized somatic alarm rather than a pursuit/persecution context. It stands apart from the other trigger items and does not connect plausibly to the memory content provided.

issues.item: Negative Appraisals: Fear Going Crazy: My reactions since the event mean that I am going crazy
issues.explanation: 'My reactions since the event mean that I am going crazy' is not well aligned with the rest of the formulation and item set. The profile otherwise emphasizes guilt, grief, misery, fragmented/numb recall, and bodily false alarms after a loved-one trauma. A 'going crazy' appraisal is possible, but here it appears weakly supported by the trigger and memory content and feels clinically out of step relative to the otherwise bereavement/guilt-focused presentation.

issues.item: Negative Appraisals: Life Not Worth Living: I am not sure my life is worth living anymore
issues.explanation: For trauma to a loved one, severe guilt, misery, and a sense that life has been destroyed can be coherent. However, the specific appraisal 'I am not sure my life is worth living anymore' is notably more global and suicidal in tone than the rest of the selected profile, and it is not supported by corresponding threat, memory, trigger, or strategy content. With the provided five components, this item stands out as insufficiently anchored to the rest of the formulation-relevant material, making the node less internally coherent.

vignette: Case Vignette for Tama Tama is a 24-year-old male of Oceania ethnicity who works as a pharmacist. He has been struggling with symptoms since the traumatic event involving the loss of his younger sister, which occurred over six months ago. The trauma was precipitated by an accident where she died while under the influence of alcohol. Since then, Tama's life has been irrevocably altered. The night of the accident remains a fragmented and emotionally charged memory for Tama. He recalls the police arriving at his door with grave news, but much of the event feels numb and distant. The senselessness of it all—his sister misbehaving, alcohol being a factor—has made every moral violation he encounters feel profoundly personal and triggering. Funerals and cemeteries have become places of intense emotional distress for him, each visit stirring up memories of his sister's death. Tama’s inability to form a coherent narrative about the event has only compounded his distress. When he tries to recount what happened, it feels as though he is telling someone else’s story, devoid of emotion and clarity. This detachment from his own memory exacerbates his triggers, making him hyper-aware of every detail that might remind him of the accident. The constant tension in Tama’s body is a physical manifestation of the emotional turmoil he experiences daily. He often finds himself reacting with heightened alertness, as if danger were always lurking just around the corner. This state of being "on alert" has become almost automatic, leaving little room for calm or joy in his life. Tama had come to believe that his life was irreparably damaged by this event. The happiness he once felt now seems like a distant memory, replaced by a sense of perpetual misery and the feeling that nothing in his life holds meaning anymore. This deep-seated belief has made it harder for him to trust his own perceptions; even when there is no actual danger, his body reacts as if it were under threat. The guilt he feels whenever he remembers the event intensifies this cycle of negative thoughts and physical reactions. He often wonders if something he could have done differently might have prevented her death, leading him to feel that every trigger—whether it be a funeral or the smell of alcohol—is a reminder of his own failure. Tama’s occupation as a pharmacist has become particularly challenging in light of these triggers. Working in an environment where alcohol is occasionally referenced has led to moments where he felt his body reacting before he even had time to think, causing him to leave work early on several occasions. These reactions have also strained his social interactions, making it difficult for him to engage with colleagues or friends without feeling anxious. The weight of these negative appraisals and the constant threat perception has taken a toll on Tama’s overall well-being. He is certain that his life will never return to what it once was, and this belief continues to reinforce his sense of vulnerability and dread. What finally brought Tama to seek help was the realization that he could no longer function effectively in his daily life without feeling overwhelmed by these symptoms. His most pressing concern is finding a way to reclaim some semblance of meaning and happiness amidst the pain and guilt, while also managing the overwhelming physical reactions that accompany his triggers. Tama's story is one of loss compounded by the relentless cycle of negative appraisals and heightened threat perception, each reinforcing the other in ways that make it difficult for him to find peace. The memories that haunt him feel both distant and intensely personal, pulling at the threads of his present life and leaving him yearning for a way back to a time when he felt whole and hopeful again.
